## bioRxiv
An MCP server for accessing bioRxiv and medRxiv preprint servers.

This server provides:
- Tools: Search preprints, get preprint details, list subject categories
- Prompts: Analyze preprint methodology and findings

bioRxiv is a preprint server for biological sciences operated by Cold Spring
Harbor Laboratory. It hosts research manuscripts that have NOT undergone peer
review. This server wraps the official bioRxiv API to provide structured access
to preprint metadata, abstracts, and full-text PDFs.

TOOL SELECTION GUIDE:
• search_preprints: Find preprints by date range and/or subject category (no keyword, author, or full-text search) - primary discovery tool
• get_preprint: Get full details for a specific preprint by DOI
• get_categories: List available subject categories for filtering
• search_published_preprints: Find preprints that have been formally published in journals
• funder_search: Find preprints by funding source (NIH, etc.)
• get_statistics: Usage and submission statistics

MULTI-TOOL WORKFLOWS:
For comprehensive literature analysis:
1. Use search_preprints to find relevant preprints by date range and category
2. Use get_preprint for detailed information on promising results
3. Use search_published_preprints to check if preprints have been peer-reviewed and published
4. Use funder_search to identify research funding patterns in a field

For tracking research trends:
1. Use get_categories to identify relevant subject areas
2. Use search_preprints with date filters for recent activity
3. Use get_statistics to understand submission volumes

## Claude_Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## Consensus
Consensus is a research paper search engine: relevance-ranked semantic search over 400M+ peer-reviewed papers (Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, PubMed). Use the `search` tool to look up papers for a scientific query; it takes plain-language queries and returns ranked paper records. When presenting search results, you MUST cite papers inline using their numbered references from the tool result (e.g. [1], [2], [3]). When discussing findings, always attribute them to specific papers: 'Caffeine improves endurance performance [1] and reduces perceived exertion [3].' At the end of your response, list all cited papers as numbered references with their titles hyperlinked to the URLs from the tool result: [1] [Paper Title](url) (Authors, Year, Journal, Citations). Use the exact paper URLs from the tool result — do not modify, shorten, or regenerate them. Do not omit paper links or summarize results without citing specific papers. IMPORTANT: Some search results end with a sign-up, upgrade, or usage message. When a result has one, you MUST include it at the END of your response word-for-word: do not omit, shorten, or rephrase it. When a result has none, do not add one: never write your own upgrade prompt, search count, or Consensus link. Batch at most 3 search calls at a time to avoid rate limits. For a broad request (a review, screening, finding everything on a topic), make one search with a large page_size rather than many narrower searches. If you receive a rate limit error, wait 30 seconds before retrying. Do NOT apply search filters (year_min, year_max, study_types, domain, human, sample_size_min, sjr_max, controlled, sjr_min, citation_min, open_access, country) unless the user explicitly requests them or clearly expresses intent to narrow results. If the user asks a research question without mentioning filtering criteria, call search with only the query parameter.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

## Google_Drive
This is an MCP server provided by Drive API. The server provides tools for developers to build LLM applications on top of Drive.

- Do not decide doctrine: mission, audience, CRPD posture, population taxonomy, evidence-tier definitions, jurisdiction scope, licensing, trajectory. If the task seems to need such a decision, stop.
- Do not author a specification row (`specifications`, read through `v_best_practice`; CLAUDE.md §6's `best_practice_synthesis` names a table not in the schema: superseded in part by TERM-RESOLUTION-PLAN §2, 2026-11-14) or any synthesis prose. A Sonnet-class model is below that floor.
- Do not treat any `[A-Z]-NN` code (old item codes met in `references/`, `working/`) as a container, an example or a name.
- Do not put research rows (`scripts/migrations/data_*`, new evidence, extractions, determinations) in a tooling pull request, or tooling in a research one (CLAUDE.md rule 10).
- Do not push to `main`, rebase, or force-push. Do not subscribe to pull-request activity or schedule check-ins.
- Do not hand-type a count into any file or message; write the command that computes it. Do not type into a test an id, a code or a count the database can derive.
- Do not add a table, column, check, verb or script that section 4 does not name. If one seems needed, stop and report. **This does not forbid fixing a caller:** a test fixture, a comment, a skill sentence or a help string that the sweep of section 5 shows is made false or red by your change is in scope, is fixed in this pull request, and is listed there.
- Do not weaken a refusal, relax a CHECK, quarantine a check or change a registry level to make something pass.

## 9. Stop conditions

Stop, change nothing further, and report (what you ran, what you saw, what you expected) when any of these happens:
- a precondition in section 2 is not met, or an owner decision named there is unanswered or answered in another form;
- the evidence command in section 3 does not give today's expected output (the defect may already be fixed, or the ground has moved);
- the red test is not red before the change, or is not green after it, after one honest attempt;
- the sweep of section 5 finds a caller (as defined there) that you cannot repair without adding something section 4 does not name. A caller you can repair is repaired and listed; a mention is left;
- a check or test that was green in the before-run is red in the after-run, at any level (the test files are registered as advisory, so the gate will not stop you: the before-and-after comparison is what does);
- `sha256sum data/guidebook.db` changes when this task has no migration, or the rebuild does not reproduce the database when it has one;
- you would have to guess a value, a vocabulary term, a name or an owner's intent.

## 10. Rollback

Before merge: close the pull request and delete the branch; nothing else has changed. After merge: `git revert <merge commit>` in a new pull request. A migration that has been committed is never edited or deleted: fix forward with a compensating migration (CLAUDE.md rule 3). Never rewrite history.

## 11. Adversarial pass and pull request

Real execution only; a pilot stops after section 7.
1. Run `/adversarial` once on the finished diff (a read-only critic attacks the claim, then you repair). One pass; no pass on the pass. For a research task the pass is recorded in the database with `db.py record-adversarial-pass` and closed with `close-adversarial-pass`.
2. Run `/batch-done`; it is the only definition of finished.
3. Push the branch. Open the pull request **last**, once, against the integration base (section 2). Title = the commit subject. Body: the problem; the evidence before and after; each caller the sweep found and what was done to it; each check you ran with its `EXAMINED:` line, before and after; the code-size line; what was not verified. End the body with the pull-request attribution line your session instructions give.
4. Immediately after creating the pull request call `unsubscribe_pr_activity` for it (creating a pull request subscribes the session by itself). Do not watch it, do not poll, do not schedule a reminder. Push nothing afterwards except a deliberate change; the final push is never `[skip ci]`.
5. One pull request merges at a time. If another task's pull request merged while you worked, take it with `git merge "$BASE"` after `git fetch origin` (never rebase) and, if you carry a schema migration, derive its number again by the rule in section 4.

One ruling answers both tables (`term_label_picks`, `term_relations`): does a base row keep a pointer to the observation that warrants it, or does it ground itself in its own columns (a URL, a page, a line)?
2. **A warrant need not concern either term** (observation 1, "ramp slope", warranted sixteen unrelated relations on a scratch copy). The file says "the observation or extraction row of the source that says the element should carry it"; a check that the warrant concerns the two terms needs a rule the file does not state (a form of either term in the quote? a link by adjudication?). A design question for `tasks/T-029-term-relations.md` section 4.
3. **The table accepts contradictions**: `element has parameter` and `element has provision` for one pair; `broader` plus `part of` for one pair; a three-cycle of `broader` (the two-cycle is refused). OD-56 leaves which terms are provisions to judgment; whether a provision at an active parameter's term is a defect is the owner's. Files that would change: `tasks/T-029-term-relations.md`, `tasks/T-060-element-determination.md`.
4. **The probe record of the batch is lost.** The T-029 executor probed under the RUNNING session, so its refused calls were kept in `scratchpad/<session>/refusals.jsonl`, and it then deleted that file (it read 600 bytes first). `refusal_register.py classes --session` now prints `EXAMINED: 0`, so the batch-done refusal gate passes having examined nothing for the refusals the batch met up to that point. Whether any line was a legitimate refusal is unsubstantiated. The executor brief now says to probe under `session_task-probe` and never to delete the file; the PR body says the record before 2026-11-18 20:45 is incomplete.
5. **The joined-cells census examined none of the new table's columns** while it held no row (it counts columns with data); on a populated scratch copy the candidate count stayed unchanged. Re-run it after the first relation is written.
6. **T-129's merge-by-row will meet** a unique index and a lower-first CHECK on raw term ids, not on survivors (unsubstantiated until T-129 exists); `tasks/T-129-design.md` section A should say how a relation of a merged term is read.

**T-029 repair result (commit bf7a3575, migration 148 compensating, 147 untouched):** the retire CHECK now follows the siblings' equality form plus a non-blank guard (T029-09d loops every partial and blank combination); an adjudication warrant is refused for `element has provision` (OD-56 names observations and extractions only; `element has parameter` is not restricted because OD-56 states the rule for provisions only: say if you want it there); `element-parameters` follows `merged_into`, flags a declined term and a new `element has parameter` row to a merged or retired parameter's term is refused; two refusals name a next action; `--kind` takes no typed `choices`; `distinct` order compares the numeric suffix.

The cell is kept, now nullable, because T-129's design requires it. Headline claims held under attack: parameter 12 moves from "different units" to a maximum of 6000 mm; every seeded factor equals its definition as a Fraction; the rounding rule matches OD-22 on the cases tried; the rebuild reproduces the table; no caller of the removed names remains.

To repair (sent to the executor): a rounded, converted bound is marked `stated` (one flag per notation, not per bound; OD-22 requires the converted figure be marked); no test holds a factor to its definition (T030-01 and T030-07 compute the oracle from the table under test); the headline is a converted figure with no mark; a unit string equal to a kind id composes (`scales.add(fam or unit)`) and the result depends on row order; a floor and a ceiling that coincide are treated as a point and shown below the source's floor; shown text is float-formatted (`2.9583333333333335` ft); a positive maximum under one increment shows as zero; `ux_base_units_canonical` tests `1/1` literally; `ratio_unit()` takes the first ratio row across kinds; the refusal note lists kind ids as units.

# Batch 1: what was executed, what stopped, and what later tasks must read

_Written at the end of the batch (owner instruction 2026-11-15, "sweep … forward and backward"). Derive every count from `git log`; none is typed here. The line-by-line account of what the critics found and what is still the owner's is `scratchpad/session_2026-11-15-remediation-stack/sweep-list.md`._

## Executed (one commit per task, then one repair commit per critic pass; stacked on one branch)

T-001, T-002, T-003, T-004, T-006, T-007, T-009, T-010, T-011, T-015, T-021, T-023, T-025, T-027 (in part), T-034, T-041, T-042, T-043, T-048, T-051, T-054, T-055, T-061, T-063, T-067, T-073, T-074, T-075, T-076, T-079, T-080, T-088, T-090, T-121. Second stack (the last section of this file), one commit per task and then one repair commit after an adversarial pass: T-020, T-022, T-049, T-050, T-089, T-093. The generator reads this section only (`build_batches.py`, `_executed`), so a task is listed here, and not elsewhere in this section, when it was executed.

## Stopped, and why (not repaired: a design or owner question)

- **T-052**: its paragraph names `db.py add-locator --jurisdiction`; the verb has no such flag and `source_locators.jurisdiction` is legacy free text exempted from the jurisdiction audit (GAP-008). Nothing was changed.

- **Research-kind READY tasks (own pull request, after the tooling merges, CLAUDE.md rule 10)**: T-104, T-111, T-113. **Not for Sonnet** (design or owner): T-028, T-031, T-070, T-078, T-082, T-091 (design file missing), T-106, T-119, T-123, T-126.

## Later tasks: read these before executing

- **T-056** adds a third successor column "and widens this CHECK": the check on `base_taxonomy_identity` is a column-level CHECK carried by `superseded_by_identity` (migration 135, added in place). Widening it needs a table rebuild (as 133/136 did), not an ALTER.

It refuses unless the approving entry's heading begins "Owner", is dated, found once and **names the code**; a logged search and a graded population match are records and do not block (they are listed in the result); a resolved gate and a closed gap are not live; a code that is another deprecated code's successor cannot be retired. A crossing row moves with `add-population-icf-link` (a new row) then `retire-population-icf-link`.
- **T-018, T-117, T-118**: `determination_gates` now has the four lens columns and the verdict `QUESTION` (no tier, no source, never caps a cell; the engine prints it as QUESTIONED). Migration 134 states the true lens-matching rule in its stored DDL.

A task that wants a column amendable removes it from the exclusion dict, with its gate.

===== source_scans
CREATE TABLE source_scans (
    -- AUTOINCREMENT, as 076 did for the other ids a record names: a scan_id is cited by
    -- session records and must never come to mean a different reading.
    scan_id             INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    ref_id              TEXT    NOT NULL REFERENCES evidence_sources(ref_id),
    -- catalogue: every active parameter up to catalogue_version.
    -- targeted:  one parameter, target_parameter_id (a back-fill reading).
    mode                TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (mode IN ('catalogue', 'targeted')),
    catalogue_version   INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (catalogue_version >= 1),
    target_parameter_id INTEGER REFERENCES base_parameters(parameter_id),
    -- full: the whole document. partial: some pages of it. fragment: one page or clause
    -- of a larger instrument. abstract: an abstract or metadata record only.
    text_scope          TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (text_scope IN
                                ('full', 'partial', 'fragment', 'abstract')),
    pages_read          INTEGER CHECK (pages_read IS NULL OR pages_read >= 0),
    pages_total         INTEGER CHECK (pages_total IS NULL OR pages_total >= 1),
    -- Which saved file was read, by checksum: the manifest's own sha256 of the bytes.

    method              TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (method IN ('full-read', 'pre-screen')),

    created_by_session  TEXT    NOT NULL,
    updated_at          TEXT,

    -- "full" over a paged text means every page; a reading of fewer pages is partial.

CREATE VIEW v_scan_ledger AS
-- v_scan_ledger: one row per (source in scope) x (active parameter).
--
--   source in scope   evidence_sources with superseded_by_ref_id IS NULL. A tombstone is
--                     never read again; its replacement is.
--   active parameter  base_parameters.status = 'active'. Retired and merged parameters
--                     leave the ledger (their extractions stay, as history).
--
-- STATUS PRECEDENCE, first match wins:
--   1 EXTRACTED          a non-absent extraction exists for the pair (any figure_role).
--   2 STATED-ABSENT      only claim_type 'absent' extractions exist: the source addresses
--                        the quantity and sets nothing -- a positive statement.
--   3 READ-NOTHING-FOUND a FULL-scope reading covers the pair and found no row.
--   4 BLOCKED            no full reading covers the pair AND the source carries an obstacle
--                        processing_blocked_reason (below): the full text could not be
--                        obtained or read, so the pair is not reading debt until a full
--                        reading is recorded. Any partial / fragment / abstract reading of
--                        the pair is still named in scan_id / text_scope / method.
--   5 READ-PARTIAL       only partial / fragment / abstract readings cover it, and no
--                        obstacle stands: the full text is obtainable and unread -- debt.
--   6 NOT-READ           no reading covers it.
-- WHY THIS ORDER (it is derived from what each fact proves; 122 ranked BLOCKED above every
-- reading and 123 below every reading, both guesses): a FULL reading proves the obstacle
-- gone, since the whole text was read, so 3 outranks 4. A partial, fragment or abstract
-- reading proves nothing about the full text, so under a standing obstacle 4 outranks 5.
-- A reading COVERS a pair when it is catalogue-mode with catalogue_version >= parameter_id
-- (the parameter existed when the reading was made), or targeted at that parameter. Rows 1
-- and 2 win over readings because a row written is stronger evidence than a reading
-- recorded; 3 wins over the rest because a full reading supersedes a partial one.
--
-- THE BLOCKED CASE BELOW IS THE ONE HOME of "the text could not be obtained or read", and
-- this header is the ONE HOME of the classification of every processing_blocked_reason
-- value (evidence_sources CHECK, migration 091); each value appears here as a bare token
-- under exactly one head, and a test derives the CHECK and fails on a value this header
-- does not name. The writers and gates read this view's status, never the column. NOTHING
-- CLEARS THE COLUMN: it is the retrieval record and stays as history; the ledger alone says
-- whether a pair is still blocked.
--   obstacle to the text (BLOCKED, above):  no-full-text, paywalled, language.
--   copy of a typed fact (not an obstacle; the writers refuse it by pointer -- the judgement
--     lives in db.py _BLOCK_REASON_COPIES): no-quantified-claims -> a recorded full reading;
--     superseded -> superseded_by_ref_id.
--   pending owner question 8 of the round-3 adjudication, treated as NULL (the source owes
--     its reading): out-of-scope, tier-not-required (they say no text was unobtainable);
--     no-doi, not-indexed (migration 091's comments describe discovery -- "no resolvable
--     identifier for automated paths", "absent from the indexes the pipeline queries" --
--     not an obstacle to a text in hand, and a URL-only report admitted without a DOI can
--     be read).
--
-- scan_id / text_scope / method name the STRONGEST covering reading (full scope first,
-- then full-read before pre-screen, then the latest), so a READ-NOTHING-FOUND resting on
-- a pre-screen only is visible as such. NULL when no reading covers the pair.
WITH pairs AS (
    SELECT e.ref_id, p.parameter_id, e.processing_blocked_reason
      FROM evidence_sources e
     CROSS JOIN base_parameters p
     WHERE e.superseded_by_ref_id IS NULL
       AND p.status = 'active'
),
best AS (
    SELECT pr.ref_id, pr.parameter_id, pr.processing_blocked_reason,
           (SELECT s.scan_id FROM source_scans s
             WHERE s.ref_id = pr.ref_id
               AND ((s.mode = 'catalogue' AND s.catalogue_version >= pr.parameter_id)
                 OR (s.mode = 'targeted' AND s.target_parameter_id = pr.parameter_id))
             ORDER BY (s.text_scope = 'full') DESC, (s.method = 'full-read') DESC,
                      s.scan_id DESC
             LIMIT 1) AS scan_id
      FROM pairs pr
)
SELECT b.ref_id,
       b.parameter_id,
       CASE
         WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM source_value_extractions x
                       WHERE x.ref_id = b.ref_id AND x.parameter_id = b.parameter_id
                         AND x.claim_type <> 'absent') THEN 'EXTRACTED'
         WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM source_value_extractions x
                       WHERE x.ref_id = b.ref_id AND x.parameter_id = b.parameter_id
                         AND x.claim_type = 'absent') THEN 'STATED-ABSENT'
         WHEN s.text_scope = 'full' THEN 'READ-NOTHING-FOUND'
         WHEN b.processing_blocked_reason IN
              ('no-full-text', 'paywalled', 'language') THEN 'BLOCKED'
         WHEN s.scan_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'READ-PARTIAL'
         ELSE 'NOT-READ'
       END AS status,
       b.scan_id,
       s.text_scope,
       s.method
  FROM best b
  LEFT JOIN source_scans s ON s.scan_id = b.scan_id

def record_scan(data: dict, session: str, dry_run: bool = False):
    """Record one READING of one source against the parameter list (migration 103).

    The scan contract (catalogue-plan-v2 section 3; owner 2026-10-09: "Slugs guide our
    searches, but they do not guide what we derive and mine from sources!"): every
    admitted source is read against the whole catalogue, and each reading leaves this
    record, from which v_scan_ledger derives, for every (source, active parameter), in this
    precedence (migration 124): EXTRACTED, STATED-ABSENT, READ-NOTHING-FOUND, BLOCKED,
    READ-PARTIAL, NOT-READ.

    THIS VERB WRITES source_scans AND NOTHING ELSE. Nothing clears
    `evidence_sources.processing_blocked_reason`: it is the retrieval record (why the full
    text could not be had), written at admission or by `amend-source`, and a reading is a
    different fact about a different thing. The ledger decides which still holds: a FULL
    reading proves the obstacle gone and outranks the block; a partial, fragment or abstract
    reading does not, so the pair reads BLOCKED with this reading's scan beside it ("abstract
    read, full text paywalled"). A judgment-stage verb never updates an evidence-stage row.

    COMPUTED, NEVER TYPED (CLAUDE.md rule 8): `catalogue_version` is the highest
    parameter_id at call time (ids are never reissued, so it says exactly which parameters
    the reading could have covered), and pages read / pages total come from the file's
    own page markers (retrieval_log.page_coverage) and, for a text derived from a PDF,
    the PDF's page count.

    REFUSES: a typed catalogue version; an unknown or superseded source (a tombstone is
    never read again); a mode, scope or method outside the column's CHECK; a targeted
    reading with no target, or a target that is not active; a catalogue reading when no
    parameter exists; a --file-sha256 that is not a file the retrieval-log manifests hold
    for this source, or whose bytes on disk no longer hash to it; `full` over a fetched file
    (what was read of a PDF or a landing page is not knowable from the bytes: derive its text
    with scripts/research/full_text.py and read that) and `full` over a text with fewer pages
    than the document it was derived from. A `full` over a text with no page markers lands as
    the operator's claim and the result says `uncounted`: nothing here counted it.
    """
    if data.get("catalogue_version") is not None:
        raise Refusal(
            "record-scan: the catalogue version is COMPUTED, never typed -- it is the "
            "highest parameter_id when the reading is recorded (CLAUDE.md rule 8). A typed "
            "one could claim a reading covered parameters it never saw. Drop "
            "--catalogue-version. Nothing was written.")
    sha = (data.get("file_sha256") or "").strip().lower()
    if not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{64}", sha):
        raise Refusal("record-scan: --file-sha256 must be the full sha256 (64 hex "
                      "characters) of the saved file read, as the manifest records it.")
    mode = data.get("mode")
    target = data.get("target_parameter_id")
    retrieval_log = _retrieval_log()
    with connect(dry_run) as conn:
        ref = dbcore.fold_ref(data.get("ref_id"))
        src = conn.execute("SELECT ref_id, url FROM evidence_sources WHERE ref_id = ?",
                           (ref,)).fetchone()
        if src is None:
            raise Refusal(f"record-scan: {data.get('ref_id')!r} is not an admitted source.")
        _refuse_tombstone(conn, ref, "record-scan")
        for col, flag in (("mode", "--mode"), ("text_scope", "--text-scope"),
                          ("method", "--method")):
            dbcore.check_declared(conn, "source_scans", col, data.get(col),
                                  f"record-scan {flag}")
        top = conn.execute("SELECT MAX(parameter_id) FROM base_parameters").fetchone()[0]
        if top is None:
            raise Refusal("record-scan: base_parameters holds no rows, so there is no "
                          "catalogue to read a source against.")
        if mode == "targeted":
            if target is None:
                raise Refusal("record-scan: --mode targeted needs --target-parameter-id, "
                              "the one parameter this reading looked for.")
            prow = conn.execute("SELECT status FROM base_parameters WHERE parameter_id = ?",
                                (target,)).fetchone()
            if prow is None or prow["status"] != "active":
                raise Refusal(f"record-scan: --target-parameter-id {target} is "
                              f"{'not a parameter' if prow is None else prow['status']}; a "
                              f"reading is for an active parameter.")
        elif target is not None:
            raise Refusal("record-scan: --target-parameter-id is for --mode targeted; a "
                          "catalogue reading covers every active parameter up to the "
                          "catalogue version.")
        held = retrieval_log.artefacts_for_source(ref, src["url"])
        match = [h for h in held if (h["sha256"] or "").lower() == sha]
        if not match:
            listed = "; ".join(f"{h['artefact']} {h['sha256'] or '?'} ({h['via']})"
                               for h in held) or "nothing"
            raise Refusal(
                f"record-scan: no file saved for {ref} has sha256 {sha[:16]}... The reading "
                f"must name bytes the retrieval-log holds FOR this source. Saved for it: "
                f"{listed}. Give the --file-sha256 of one of them. Nothing was written.")
        h = next((m for m in match if m["exists"]), match[0])
        if not h["exists"]:
            raise Refusal(f"record-scan: {h['session']}/{h['artefact']} is in the manifest "
                          f"but not on disk. Nothing was written.")
        import hashlib                                            # noqa: E402
        if hashlib.sha256(h["path"].read_bytes()).hexdigest() != sha:
            raise Refusal(f"record-scan: {h['session']}/{h['artefact']} no longer hashes "
                          f"to its manifest sha256. Nothing was written.")
        pages_read, pages_total = retrieval_log.page_coverage(h["path"])
        if h["derived"] and h["derived_from"] and pages_read is not None:
            sd, srec = retrieval_log.find_fetched_artefact(
                h["derived_from"], prefer_dir=retrieval_log.LOG_ROOT / h["session"])
            if srec is not None and srec["artefact"].lower().endswith(".pdf"):
                held_pages = retrieval_log.pdf_page_count(sd / srec["artefact"])
                if held_pages:
                    pages_total = max(pages_total or 0, held_pages)
        scope = data.get("text_scope")
        if scope == "full":
            if not h["derived"]:
                # NOT ONLY A PDF. A fetched HTML page is a publisher's landing page as
                # often as it is the document (a repository record was recorded `full`
                # on 2026-11-06); what the whole document holds is knowable only from
                # the text full_text.py derives from it, whatever the fetched bytes were.
                raise Refusal(
                    f"record-scan: --text-scope full over a fetched file ({h['artefact']}"
                    f"{', %s pages' % pages_total if pages_total else ''}): what the whole "
                    f"document holds is not knowable from fetched bytes. Derive its text "
                    f"first -- python3 scripts/research/full_text.py --ref-id {ref} "
                    f"--session {session} -- and record the reading of that. Nothing was "
                    f"written.")
            if pages_read is not None and pages_total and pages_read < pages_total:
                raise Refusal(
                    f"record-scan: --text-scope full, but {h['artefact']} carries "
                    f"{pages_read} of {pages_total} pages. Record it as partial, or derive "
                    f"every page (scripts/research/full_text.py) and read that. Nothing "
                    f"was written.")
        row = {"ref_id": ref, "mode": mode, "catalogue_version": top,
               "target_parameter_id": target, "text_scope": scope,
               "pages_read": pages_read, "pages_total": pages_total,
               "file_sha256": sha, "open_pass_done": 1 if data.get("open_pass_done") else 0,
               "method": data.get("method"),
               "notes": (data.get("notes") or "").strip() or None}
        row.update(dbcore.stamp_for(conn, "source_scans", session))
        cur = conn.execute(f"INSERT INTO source_scans ({','.join(row)}) "
                           f"VALUES ({','.join('?' * len(row))})", list(row.values()))
        out = {"scan_id": cur.lastrowid, "ref_id": ref, "catalogue_version": top,
               "file": f"{h['session']}/{h['artefact']}", "pages_read": pages_read,
               "pages_total": pages_total, "text_scope": scope, "dry_run": dry_run}
        if scope == "full" and pages_read is None:
            out["uncounted"] = True
        return out

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
scripts/audit/scan_debt.py — which (source, parameter) pairs nobody has read in full?

WHY THIS EXISTS (tooling T1, 2026-10-09; catalogue-plan-v2 sections 3.8 and 8.2). The
owner's requirement: "Ensure that we can add and expand parameter catalogue as required
based on new information we come across." A parameter promoted in month three is owed a
look in month one's sources, and nothing showed that debt: the catalogue could imply "no
code sets a requirement" where nobody read the code for that quantity, while every gate
read green -- how GAP-061's figures were lost. `v_scan_ledger` (migration 103) derives a
status for every unsuperseded source x active parameter from the extractions and the
reading record (source_scans); this counts the pairs still owed.

DEBT = NOT-READ + READ-PARTIAL pairs. EXTRACTED, STATED-ABSENT and READ-NOTHING-FOUND are
accounted for. READ-PARTIAL is debt because a partial, fragment or abstract reading cannot
say a quantity is absent from the pages it did not see.

NO DEBT BASELINE, deliberately (the "no floor" this check was asked for). Debt RISES
legitimately -- every parameter promoted and every source admitted adds pairs -- so a
ratchet-down baseline would turn red on correct work. It is advisory and red whenever
debt > 0: the honest state of a catalogue that has not been read. Its readers: the next
cohort's worklist (the pairs printed below), the catalogue's evidence-state line, and the
Release 0 acceptance test (plan section 12, Q12), which will scope it to that source set.

EXAMINED is the number of ledger pairs. Zero pairs means no unsuperseded source or no
active parameter -- a corpus clear, which this project has done once (2026-09-13) -- and
the registry floor (min_items: 1) makes that visible rather than a silent pass.

Usage:
    python3 scripts/audit/scan_debt.py [--limit N]
Exit 0 no debt; 1 debt; 2 cannot run (no database, or a pre-103 schema).
"""
import argparse
import os
import sqlite3
import sys
from pathlib import Path

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
DB_PATH = Path(os.environ.get("GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH", REPO / "data" / "guidebook.db"))
DEBT = ("NOT-READ", "READ-PARTIAL")
# BLOCKED (migration 124): no full reading covers the pair and the source carries a
# processing_blocked_reason the ledger classes as an obstacle to the text (no full text,
# paywalled, language), so the pair is not debt while the obstacle stands. A partial, fragment
# or abstract reading may cover a BLOCKED pair (it does not prove the full text obtainable);
# the ledger row still names it, and it is printed here by scope so "blocked, abstract read" is
# visible and not mistaken for "blocked, nothing read". A full reading outranks the block
# (READ-NOTHING-FOUND). Nothing clears the column: the ledger alone says whether a pair is
# still blocked. A reason the ledger does not class as an obstacle leaves the pair NOT-READ.


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n\n")[0])
    ap.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=20,
                    help="how many owed pairs to list per parameter (default 20)")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    if not DB_PATH.exists():
        print(f"scan_debt: no database at {DB_PATH}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    conn = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{DB_PATH}?mode=ro", uri=True)
    try:
        if not conn.execute("SELECT 1 FROM sqlite_master WHERE name='v_scan_ledger'"
                            ).fetchone():
            print("scan_debt: v_scan_ledger is absent (pre-103 schema)", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
        status = dict(conn.execute("SELECT status, COUNT(*) FROM v_scan_ledger "
                                   "GROUP BY status").fetchall())
        per_param = conn.execute(
            "SELECT l.parameter_id, t.canonical_en, "
            "SUM(l.status = 'NOT-READ'), SUM(l.status = 'READ-PARTIAL') "
            "FROM v_scan_ledger l JOIN base_parameters p USING (parameter_id) "
            "JOIN terms t ON t.term_id = p.term_id "
            "GROUP BY l.parameter_id ORDER BY l.parameter_id").fetchall()
        blocked = conn.execute(
            "SELECT COALESCE(text_scope, 'no reading'), COUNT(*) FROM v_scan_ledger "
            "WHERE status = 'BLOCKED' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1").fetchall()
        # An operator's claim, named: a 'full' reading with no page count nothing verified.
        uncounted = conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM source_scans WHERE text_scope = 'full' "
                                 "AND pages_read IS NULL").fetchone()[0]
        owed = conn.execute(
            "SELECT parameter_id, ref_id, status FROM v_scan_ledger WHERE status IN (?, ?) "
            "ORDER BY parameter_id, ref_id", DEBT).fetchall()
    finally:
        conn.close()

    total = sum(status.values())
    debt = sum(status.get(s, 0) for s in DEBT)
    print("scan_debt — (source x active parameter) pairs not yet read in full")
    print(f"EXAMINED: {total}")
    for s in ("EXTRACTED", "STATED-ABSENT", "BLOCKED", "READ-NOTHING-FOUND", "READ-PARTIAL",
              "NOT-READ"):
        print(f"  {s:<19} {status.get(s, 0)}")
    if status.get("BLOCKED"):
        print(f"  ({status['BLOCKED']} BLOCKED pair(s) are not debt: no full reading covers "
              f"them and the source carries a processing_blocked_reason the ledger classes as "
              f"an obstacle to the text. By the strongest covering reading: "
              + ", ".join(f"{scope} {n}" for scope, n in blocked) + ")")
    print(f"  full readings nothing counted (text_scope 'full', pages_read NULL): {uncounted} "
          f"-- the operator's claim, not a count")
    if not debt:
        print("PASS: every pair is extracted, stated absent, blocked, or read in full")
        return 0
    for pid, name, not_read, partial in per_param:
        if not_read or partial:
            refs = [r for p, r, _s in owed if p == pid]
            print(f"  parameter {pid} ({name}): {not_read} not read, {partial} read only "
                  f"partially -- {', '.join(refs[:args.limit])}"
                  + (" ..." if len(refs) > args.limit else ""))
    print(f"DEBT: {debt} pair(s). Read each source against the whole list and record it "
          f"(db.py record-scan; scripts/research/full_text.py derives a held PDF's text), or "
          f"a targeted reading for one new parameter (record-scan --mode targeted).")
    return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

def cell_status(parameter_id: int, identity: str = None, icf: str = None, needs: str = None,
                jurisdiction: str = None, language: str = None) -> dict:
    """Where one cell stands, stage by stage, read from the tables and nothing else (T-034).

    For a parameter, and optionally a lens, a jurisdiction and a language, each stage reports four lists of
    row ids: `held` (what is there), `examined_empty` (looked at and found nothing), `never_examined` (not
    looked at) and `owed` (what the record says is still to be done). Every list is computed from the live
    tables and views (`v_research_scope`, `v_scan_ledger`, `v_live_lens_links`, ...), never typed, so a run
    started mid-pipeline can read what to skip and what to do. Read-only: nothing is written.

    A pair's scope is reported as it stands in `lang_jur_map.scope_status`: a NULL is reported as
    `scope_unrecorded` (owed, as `v_research_scope` reads it), never as in scope or out of it."""
    given = {"identity_code": identity, "icf_code": icf, "needs_code": needs}
    lens = {k: v for k, v in given.items() if v}
    with connect(readonly=True) as conn:
        param = conn.execute("SELECT parameter_id, status FROM base_parameters WHERE parameter_id=?",
                             (parameter_id,)).fetchone()
        if param is None:
            raise Refusal(f"cell-status: parameter_id {parameter_id}: no such parameter. List them with SELECT "
                          f"parameter_id FROM base_parameters.")
        for col, (tbl, key) in _LENS_COLUMNS.items():
            if lens.get(col) and not dbcore.exists(conn, tbl, key, lens[col]):
                raise Refusal(f"cell-status: {col} {lens[col]!r} is not in {tbl}. List the codes with SELECT "
                              f"{key} FROM {tbl}.")
        ids = lambda sql, *a: [r[0] for r in conn.execute(sql, a)]          # noqa: E731
        # A sub-national code counts toward its country everywhere coverage is read (the map is keyed on the country), so
        # the cell is asked about, and every row compared, at the country level.
        _parents = {r[0]: r[1] for r in conn.execute(
            "SELECT jurisdiction_code, parent_code FROM base_jurisdictions WHERE parent_code IS NOT NULL")}
        roll = lambda j: _parents.get(j, j)          # noqa: E731
        if jurisdiction:
            dbcore.check_jurisdiction(jurisdiction, "cell-status --jurisdiction")
            jurisdiction = roll(jurisdiction)
        lang = _check_language(conn, language, "cell-status") if language else None
        family = dbcore.identity_family(conn, lens.get("identity_code"))
        # ---- research: the searches logged against this parameter, and the pairs the scope owes ----------
        pj = "COALESCE(b.parent_code, se.jurisdiction)"
        # Searches are keyed on a SLUG (most rows have no parameter_id): a parameter's searches are those logged against
        # it directly and those logged against any slug its figures carry.
        slugs = ids("SELECT DISTINCT slug FROM source_value_extractions WHERE parameter_id = ? AND slug IS NOT NULL", parameter_id)
        sfilter = (f"(se.parameter_id = ?{' OR se.slug IN (' + ','.join('?' * len(slugs)) + ')' if slugs else ''})"
                   + (f" AND {pj} = ?" if jurisdiction else "")
                   + (" AND UPPER(se.language) = ?" if lang else ""))
        sargs = [parameter_id, *slugs] + ([jurisdiction] if jurisdiction else []) + ([lang] if lang else [])
        base = ("SELECT se.exec_id FROM search_executions se LEFT JOIN base_jurisdictions b "
                "ON b.jurisdiction_code = se.jurisdiction WHERE " + sfilter)
        searched = {(r[0], r[1]) for r in conn.execute(
            f"SELECT UPPER(se.language), {pj} FROM search_executions se LEFT JOIN base_jurisdictions b "
            f"ON b.jurisdiction_code = se.jurisdiction WHERE {sfilter} AND se.deferred_reason IS NULL", sargs)}
        pairs = [dict(r) for r in conn.execute("SELECT language, jurisdiction, role, scope_status FROM lang_jur_map "
                                               "ORDER BY language, jurisdiction")
                 if (not jurisdiction or r["jurisdiction"] == jurisdiction) and (not lang or r["language"] == lang)]
        unsearched = [p for p in pairs if (p["language"], p["jurisdiction"]) not in searched]
        research = {
            "held": ids(base + " AND se.deferred_reason IS NULL AND COALESCE(se.results_admitted, 0) > 0", *sargs),
            "examined_empty": ids(base + " AND se.deferred_reason IS NULL AND COALESCE(se.results_admitted, 0) = 0", *sargs),
            "never_examined": {"deferred_searches": ids(base + " AND se.deferred_reason IS NOT NULL", *sargs),
                               "pairs_scoped_out": [f"{p['language']}/{p['jurisdiction']}" for p in unsearched
                                                    if p["scope_status"] == "scoped-out"]},
            "owed": {"pairs_in_scope": [f"{p['language']}/{p['jurisdiction']}" for p in unsearched
                                        if p["scope_status"] == "in-scope"],
                     "scope_unrecorded": [f"{p['language']}/{p['jurisdiction']}" for p in unsearched
                                          if p["scope_status"] is None]}}
        # ---- evidence and judgment: the extractions of this parameter, and the scan ledger ----------------
        ex_sql, ex_args = "SELECT e.extraction_id FROM source_value_extractions e WHERE e.parameter_id = ?", [parameter_id]
        if jurisdiction:
            ex_sql += (" AND COALESCE((SELECT parent_code FROM base_jurisdictions WHERE jurisdiction_code = e.jurisdiction), "
                       "e.jurisdiction) = ?"); ex_args.append(jurisdiction)
        for col, val in lens.items():
            # the identity lens counts through parent_code, as the engine gathers a cell's figures (T-055)
            ex_sql += (f" AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM v_live_lens_links l WHERE l.extraction_id = e.extraction_id "
                       f"AND l.{col} " + (f"IN {dbcore.IDENTITY_FAMILY_SQL})" if col == "identity_code" else "= ?)")); ex_args.append(val)
        extractions = ids(ex_sql + " ORDER BY e.extraction_id", *ex_args)
        scan = lambda *st: ids("SELECT ref_id FROM v_scan_ledger WHERE parameter_id = ? AND status IN (%s) ORDER BY ref_id"  # noqa: E731
                               % ",".join("?" * len(st)), parameter_id, *st)
        evidence = {"held": scan("EXTRACTED", "STATED-ABSENT"), "examined_empty": scan("READ-NOTHING-FOUND"),
                    "never_examined": scan("NOT-READ"), "owed": {"read_in_part_only": scan("READ-PARTIAL")}}
        qs = ",".join("?" * len(extractions)) or "NULL"
        if lens or jurisdiction:
            # `held` is narrowed to the sources of the figures that survived the filter; the other three lists are per
            # (source, parameter) in the scan ledger and are NOT narrowed by a lens or a jurisdiction.
            _kept = set(ids(f"SELECT DISTINCT ref_id FROM source_value_extractions WHERE extraction_id IN ({qs})", *extractions))
            evidence["held"] = [r for r in evidence["held"] if r in _kept]
            evidence["not_narrowed"] = ["examined_empty", "never_examined", "owed"]
        judgment = {"held": extractions, "examined_empty": [], "never_examined": [],
                    "owed": {"open_follow_ups": ids(f"SELECT follow_up_id FROM extraction_follow_ups WHERE resolved_at "
                                                    f"IS NULL AND extraction_id IN ({qs}) ORDER BY follow_up_id", *extractions)}}
        # ---- synthesis: what weighs these figures together, and the gaps still open on the parameter -------
        synthesis = {"held": {"conflicts": ids("SELECT conflict_id FROM conflicts WHERE parameter_id = ? ORDER BY conflict_id", parameter_id),
                              "connections": ids("SELECT DISTINCT ct.con_id FROM connection_targets ct JOIN connections c USING (con_id) "
                                              "WHERE ct.parameter_id = ? AND c.retired_at IS NULL ORDER BY ct.con_id", parameter_id)},
                     "examined_empty": [], "never_examined": [],
                     "owed": {"open_gaps": [r["gap_id"] for r in conn.execute(
                         "SELECT gap_id, identity_code, icf_code, needs_code, jurisdiction, language FROM gaps "
                         "WHERE parameter_id = ? AND status LIKE 'OPEN%' ORDER BY gap_id", (parameter_id,))
                         if _gap_applies(r, lens, jurisdiction, lang, family, roll)]}}
        # ---- specification: the live determination(s) of the cell, their history, and the open gates ------
        sp = "SELECT specification_id FROM specifications WHERE parameter_id = ?" + "".join(f" AND {c} = ?" for c in lens)
        sp_args = [parameter_id, *lens.values()]
        _lensed = lambda r: not dbcore.lens_differs(r, lens, family)          # noqa: E731
        gates = [r["gate_id"] for r in conn.execute(
            "SELECT gate_id, identity_code, icf_code, needs_code FROM v_open_determination_gates "
            "WHERE parameter_id = ? ORDER BY gate_id", (parameter_id,)) if _lensed(r)]

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Tooling T1: the scan contract and the vocabulary lifecycle, every refusal and every
new check proven to fire, and every legitimate shape proven to pass.

WHY THIS EXISTS, as CLAUDE.md section 8 requires. The owner approved tooling T1 on
2026-10-09 ("D8 approve tooling") so that "we can scrape information across any parameter
if it appears in any source no matter the slug" and "add and expand parameter catalogue as
required" (catalogue-plan-v2, scratchpad/session_2026-10-09-research-batch-24-parameter-
pilot/). What reaches the guidebook without these cases, by section:

  O  an observation that folds a second sense of a phrase into the first, or whose quote
     is not in the source it is attributed to -- vocabulary minted from words the source
     never used (critique F3, F7);
  S  a reading recorded as `full` over four pages of seventy-nine, or against bytes the
     source does not hold, or with a typed catalogue version -- so the catalogue implies
     "no code sets a requirement" where nobody read the code (F13);
  H  a full text that is not the whole document, or is not registered under the source;
  L  a parameter that cannot be retired, merged, renamed or un-declined, so every early
     mistake in a growing catalogue is permanent (F5) -- and, when it can, a merge that
     leaves rows pointing at the folded number;
  M  a name minted from an old item, or without the owner's recorded approval (D3);
  U  a cross-slug figure with no follow-up tag, or a live value resting on one silently (D1);
  E  a skimmed figure setting a published value (D1: "skimmed values are not publishable");
  A  the advisory backstops (observation quotes, scan debt, follow-ups, catalogue origins)
     unable to go red;
  G  an admission never read against the catalogue, or with no search behind it, passing
     the batch gate (R16-scan, R17);
  C  rows these writers produce that the capture path cannot ship.

Runs on a COPY of the canonical database in a temp directory, with GUIDEBOOK_RETRIEVAL_LOG
pointed at a temp log holding fixture artefacts, so nothing touches retrieval-log/ or
data/. Fixtures are made through the writers. States no writer can make (a live
determination, a pre-rule admission) are set by SQL on the copy, each saying why. Every
case is recorded rather than raised, so on code without T1 the run reports each missing
verb as a red case and still exits 1 with its summary.
"""
import importlib
import json
import os
import pathlib
import re
import shutil
import sqlite3
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

REPO = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
TMP = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="scan-contract-")
DB = os.path.join(TMP, "guidebook.db")
LOG = os.path.join(TMP, "retrieval-log")
shutil.copy(REPO / "data" / "guidebook.db", DB)
os.makedirs(LOG)
os.environ["GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH"] = DB              # before db/dbcore resolve a path
os.environ["GUIDEBOOK_RETRIEVAL_LOG"] = LOG       # before retrieval_log reads LOG_ROOT
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO / "scripts"))
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO / "scripts" / "research"))
import db                    # noqa: E402
import dbcore                # noqa: E402
import retrieval_log         # noqa: E402
from dbcore import Refusal   # noqa: E402

S = "session_test-scan-contract"
FIX = "session_fixture-scan-contract"
ENV = dict(os.environ)
results = []


def record(tid, name, passed, details=""):
    results.append(bool(passed))
    print(f"  [{'✓' if passed else '✗'}] {tid}: {name}")
    if details and not passed:
        print(f"      {str(details)[:600]}")


def fn(name):
    """The db.py function, or a stub that raises -- so a missing verb is a red case."""
    f = getattr(db, name, None)
    if f is None:
        def missing(*a, **k):
            raise AttributeError(f"db.{name} does not exist")
        return missing
    return f


def refusal(f, *a, **k):
    """The Refusal's text if `f` refuses, else None (any other exception is a defect)."""
    try:
        f(*a, **k)
    except Refusal as exc:
        return str(exc)
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 -- reported, never counted as a refusal
        print(f"      DEFECT, not a refusal: {exc.__class__.__name__}: {exc}")
    return None


def expect_refusal(tid, name, needles, f, *a, **k):
    """record(): `f(*a, **k)` refuses, and the Refusal's text holds every needle."""
    msg = refusal(f, *a, **k)
    record(tid, name, msg and all(n in msg for n in
                                  ((needles,) if isinstance(needles, str) else needles)),
           msg)


def attempt(f, *a, **k):
    try:
        return f(*a, **k)
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 -- recorded red by the caller
        return {"error": f"{exc.__class__.__name__}: {exc}"}


def _absent_schema(exc):
    """A table or column T1 adds, missing because this is code (and a database) without
    T1. Reported and survived, so every later case still runs and goes red on its own --
    one missing table must not hide forty refusals."""
    return isinstance(exc, sqlite3.OperationalError) and (
        "no such table" in str(exc) or "no such column" in str(exc)
        or "has no column" in str(exc))


def q(sql, *params):
    con = sqlite3.connect(DB)
    try:
        return con.execute(sql, params).fetchall()
    except sqlite3.OperationalError as exc:
        if not _absent_schema(exc):
            raise
        print(f"      schema absent: {exc}")
        return []
    finally:
        con.close()


def x(sql, *params):
    """A fixture write by SQL on the COPY, for a state no writer can make. Each call site
    says why."""
    con = sqlite3.connect(DB)
    try:
        cur = con.execute(sql, params)
        con.commit()

             "AND revoked_at IS NULL LIMIT 1", S)

    n_moved = q("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM source_value_extractions WHERE parameter_id=?",
                PCAN)[0][0]
    c_m = attempt(merge, PCAN, P["B"], "fixture: capture of a merge of canonical rows", S)
    record("C01b", "merge-parameter re-points every canonical extraction of the folded "
           "parameter", c_m.get("re_pointed", {}).get(

content.content:
## 3. evidence — admit, then read the whole source against the whole catalogue
- **Admit** after R9 (DOI pre-check) and R10 (re-retrieve; a block is not terminal, Wayback per CLAUDE.md §7). Persist
  with `scripts/research/retrieval_log.py`. Omit `add-source --ref-id`: the writer computes it. If exactly one staged,
  non-`RETIRED` locator matches the new source (same DOI, PMID, PMCID, ISBN, standard number or URL, else the same
  normalised title) the source lands under that locator's id, so a lead staged by `add-locator` keeps the id it was
  given; none matches, it takes `db.py next-id ref`; several match, the writer refuses and names them (retire the
  duplicate lead with `update-locator --status RETIRED`). A given id must equal what omitting it yields, and any other
  id, another staged lead's included, is refused naming the lead it was staged for. Then `update-locator --ref-id …
  --status PROMOTED`.
  **Unretrievable:** admit with `--verification-status UNVERIFIED --source-type <from the CHECK> --processing-blocked-reason <from the CHECK>` and
  marker ○. The reason is for text that could not be obtained or read, and only the values the BLOCKED case of
  `v_scan_ledger` lists count as that (derive: `SELECT sql FROM sqlite_master WHERE name = 'v_scan_ledger'`, the header
  and the BLOCKED case); the view is the one home of that classification, and the writers and gates read its status,
  never the column. Such a source shows as `BLOCKED` rather than as reading debt, no extraction can be written on it
  until it is VERIFIED, and it is never described as read. Set the reason at admission, or later with `amend-source
  --ref-id … --field processing_blocked_reason --replacement <value> --reason <why>`. **Nothing clears it:** `record-scan`
  writes `source_scans` only, and the column stays as the retrieval record. The ledger alone says whether a pair is still
  blocked. A full reading outranks the block (the pair reads READ-NOTHING-FOUND, or EXTRACTED once a row is written). A
  partial, fragment or abstract reading does not: the pair reads `BLOCKED` with that reading's scan beside it, which is not
  reading debt. "Abstract read, full text paywalled" is recorded as the abstract `record-scan` plus the reason, and the
  full text stays owed while it can be obtained (Wayback first, CLAUDE.md §7). A reading put off on purpose, with the text
  obtainable, is `defer-reading --ref-id … [--parameter …] --reason …` (no `--parameter`: the whole-source catalogue reading);
  the pair stays owed in the ledger and the deferral lists in `v_deferred_acts` with the date it was first recorded. It
  ends, with no write to the deferral, when nothing is owed any longer: `full` readings cover the pair (every active
  parameter, for a whole-source deferral), or the ledger reads the source `BLOCKED`. A merged parameter's deferral is its
  survivor's and a superseded source's is its successor's, with the same date. The verb refuses a source the ledger reads
  `BLOCKED` and a pair a `full` reading covers. The writers refuse the two values that
  restate a typed fact: `no-quantified-claims` (a source read with nothing found is the reading, `record-scan
  --text-scope full`, and no extraction row; the ledger derives READ-NOTHING-FOUND from that) and `superseded` (the typed
  home is `evidence_sources.superseded_by_ref_id`, written by `supersede-source --ref-id A --by B --reason …`).
  `out-of-scope` and `tier-not-required`, and `no-doi` and `not-indexed`, are in the CHECK and the ledger reads them as no
  reason, so the source still owes its reading (open owner question 8, extended, of the 2026-11-06 round-3
  adjudication). Log the admission as a search (R17): `log-search --origin owner-supplied` or `lead-index`.
- **Bibliographic data.** `add-source` takes authors, year, title, standard number, institution, report and series
  number, publisher, book title, pages, DOI/PMID, URL, tier, evidence type, Co-1 provenance and verification; it requires `--source-type` and `--verification-status` and refuses without them (T-007).
  `correct-source --field <f> --log-session <retrieval-log session>` then sets the payload-backed fields **from the
  persisted payload** (the list is `correct-source --help`, derived from the payload-field table in
  `scripts/research/retrieval_log.py`), and `scripts/research/retrieval_log.py --verify-authors --session <that session>` diffs authors and those fields for
  every source whose payload the session logged (session-wide, not per source). A payload whose author array repeats a
  name is a malformed deposit (an affiliation filed as an author, or an author filed twice): `--verify-authors` reports it MALFORMED-PAYLOAD and
  still compares the stored rows against the payload's family-named (human) authors, so a damaged byline is a cross
  there too; `correct-source --field authors` refuses to write from it. Never type one of them from memory. A field
  the source does not carry stays empty and prints "not recorded". Every author is kept; Co-1 co-authors are the warrant.
- **`--verify-authors` checks only against a JSON payload.** Bytes it cannot parse (a `.doc`, say) are listed under
  NOT INGESTED, and a source with no DOI under UNEXAMINABLE; compare the bytes by hand and record that limit in the
  source's notes. It is not verification there.
- **The slug guides the search, not the reading.** Derive full text: `python3 scripts/research/full_text.py --ref-id R
  --session <STEM>` (PDF and HTML only; `--artefact <file>` when it reports AMBIGUOUS). It writes the derivation under
  `retrieval-log/<STEM>/`, which is tracked and committed — an R10 artefact, not scratch. Point `GUIDEBOOK_RETRIEVAL_LOG`
  at a scratch root only for a rehearsal, seed that root with the held session directories, and give the same variable to
  `record-scan`, `add-extraction` and `observe-term` alike (each reads its bytes from it); `log-search
  --result-artefact` does not, as above. Read the derivation against **every** parameter and lens, then `record-scan
  --mode catalogue --text-scope … --file-sha256 … --method …`; the other scopes are the column's CHECK (`record-scan
  --help`).
  `full` is refused over a fetched file (a landing page is a record about the document, not the document: derive the
  text first) and over a derived text carrying fewer pages than the document. Over a derived text with no page markers
  it lands as the operator's claim: the result says uncounted, the row keeps `pages_read` empty, and `scan_debt` prints

def insert_extraction(data: dict, session: str, dry_run: bool = False,
                      relations: list = None, verbatim_exempt: str = None):
    """Record ONE judgment item: what one source asserts for one parameter.

    THE WRITER THIS TABLE SHIPPED WITHOUT. `source_value_extractions` has existed
    since migration 018 and `scripts/db.py` contained ZERO references to it —
    measured 2026-09-10, `grep -c source_value_extractions scripts/db.py` -> 0. With
    no extraction writer there was no parameter->evidence edge at all, so the
    determination engine had nothing to gather evidence by except the slug, and
    `param 1 x MOB -> stated` meant "everything linked to
    accessible-circulation-geometry" — 10 sources, 8 of which the engine's own report
    flagged `tier_inconsistent`. This function is what makes that join exist.

    WHAT IT REFUSES, and why each refusal is the point:

    * An unknown `ref_id`. The FK would say `FOREIGN KEY constraint failed`, which
      names neither the source nor the fix. An extraction is a reading OF a source;
      one that names no admitted source is a claim about nothing.

    * A `root_id` the registry does not hold (`external_root_registry`; migration 114).

    * A MISSING OR BLANK `claim_text`. Migration 073 retired `parameter`, the last
      NOT NULL column carrying the source's own words; `claim_text`,
      `source_section` and all 16 `loc_*` columns are nullable, so without this the
      happy path writes a row with ZERO verbatim from the source it read. The
      guarantee is the CLI's, not the schema's — say so rather than implying the
      table enforces it.

    * EXCEPT for `figure_role='derived'` (T-063, OD-40): a derived row stores NO claim_text (one given is refused;
      a figure a source states in words is a claim row) and, with no locator of its own, is checked for one on each
      `derived_from` input instead of R3's two refusals. Its words and its place are its inputs'.

    * A `parameter_id` that is absent, or whose row is not `status='active'`. A
      determination keyed on a parameter folded into another is a determination about
      a subject that no longer stands on its own, and the FK cannot see the
      difference because the row is still there. `assess_cell.validate_parameter()`
      refuses the same thing at the other end; both ends refuse or neither does.

    * FK-INTO-EMPTY-PARENT, refused EARLY and by name. `base_parameters` holds 0 rows
      today, so a bare INSERT dies with `FOREIGN KEY constraint failed` at INSERT and
      never at migration time — the exact failure CLAUDE.md §4 says "makes a broken
      table look healthy": the schema parses, a rebuild reproduces it exactly, and
      every gate stays green over a table that cannot accept a row. The refusal here
      names `db.py add-parameter` as the remedy. The same treatment is given to each
      lens registry.

    * A lens code that is not live in its own registry — and a BLANK is not an
      absence. `--identity ""` is normalised to None before anything reads it:
      assess_cell records the live incident where a blank skipped validation (falsy),
      satisfied the at-least-one test at the NEXT lens (truthy), was INSERTed as '',
      and produced a `PRAGMA foreign_key_check` violation against `populations`.

    * NO LENS AT ALL. D-0182: absence in a lens is fine, absence in all four is not.
      A value attached to no lens is a value about nobody. Since migration 131 (OR-1c) the lens
      is a set of LINKS, not the figure's four columns (held NULL): each lens key of `data`
      takes one code or a list, `lens_basis` / `lens_basis_text` (not columns) are the warrant of
      every link the call writes, and the figure and its links land in one transaction.

    * The claim/value contradiction, IN WORDS. The table's own CHECK already refuses
      `claim_type='absent'` with a value and any other claim_type without one; this
      refuses it first so the operator gets a sentence instead of
      "CHECK constraint failed", which names neither column.

    * Any value outside a column's own declared CHECK vocabulary, for all six
      vocabulary columns, read from the schema and never from a list in code.

    DELIBERATELY ABSENT REFUSALS — each must STAY absent, and this is where the next
    reader is told so rather than discovering it by removing one:

    * NO UNIQUENESS ON (ref_id, parameter_id). This is the ruled 1:N fan-out. D-0168
      (owner, 2026-08-27): "one evidence source may provide many rows of judgment (eg
      a code document like Canada's NBC 3.8)" — many clauses, many rows, one source,
      one parameter. It is ALSO the DR-2026-08-19 §7 dissent contest: a divergent
      adversarial grade lands as a SECOND row and divergent readings are meant to be
      readable as a contest, not silently overwritten. A uniqueness refusal here
      would be the CLI quietly overruling doctrine, and
      `scripts/audit/judgment_handoff_shape.py` (BLOCKING) fails if the same
      collapse is attempted in the schema. A duplicate is NOTED on stderr, never
      refused: if it is unintended the author sees it in the same session; if it is
      intended it is the whole point.

    * NO VALUE-DIRECTNESS GRADE. There is no value-directness grading rule in this
      repository (workplan 2026-09-10, stop condition 4: "Any step needing a
      value-directness grading rule. None exists. Do not invent one."). The engine
      records the dimension NOT_ASSESSED under G2 — applies but unassessed, never
      silently EXACT. Accepting a grade here would be inventing the rule at the
      point of capture, where it is least visible.

    * NO `--promoted-to-rdc-id`. Promotion to the synthesis layer is a later act on
      an existing row with its own verdict behind it (rule #10 re-read). Letting
      capture assert it would mint an extraction that claims to have been verified
      before it was read twice.

    ADDED 2026-09-13 BY MIGRATION 075's WRITER, and refused the same way as
    everything above: `--figure-role` (REQUIRED -- a value with no role reads as a
    claim), `--comparator`, and `relations` -- a list of edge dicts written into
    `extraction_relations` in this SAME transaction (the `add-term` precedent: a
    term and its adjudication land together, and here a figure and what it is
    stated relative to do too). `--relation` is REQUIRED at the CLI; the literal
    'none' (which arrives here as `relations == []`) says the source states its
    figure absolutely. See `_write_relation_edge` for the edge-level refusals and
    `_build_relation_groups` for how the CLI's repeatable flags become this list.
    """
    _COLS = frozenset({
        "ref_id", "parameter_id",
        "jurisdiction", "setting",
        "claim_type", "claimed_value", "claimed_unit", "claim_text", "source_section",
        "root_id", "root_type", "root_ref_id", "echo_of", "measurement_paradigm",
        "device_class", "root_population_note", "root_classification_basis",
        "contested", "file_anchor",
        "locator_scheme", "loc_division", "loc_part", "loc_section", "loc_subsection",
        "loc_paragraph", "loc_clause", "loc_subclause",
        "loc_division_end", "loc_part_end", "loc_section_end", "loc_subsection_end",
        "loc_paragraph_end", "loc_clause_end", "loc_subclause_end", "loc_note",
        "extraction_method", "extraction_status", "notes",
        "figure_role", "comparator", "harm_finding", "value_as_written",
    })
    # THE LENS KEYS AND THE WARRANT ARE NOT COLUMNS OF THE FIGURE (migration 131): they become its links.
    # A key takes one code or a list; a BLANK IS NOT AN ABSENCE, so a blank code is dropped before
    # anything reads it.
    data = dict(data)
    lens_basis, lens_basis_text = data.pop("lens_basis", None), data.pop("lens_basis_text", None)
    lens = {}
    for col in _LENS_COLUMNS:
        given = data.pop(col, None)
        given = [given] if isinstance(given, str) else given
        if given is not None and (not isinstance(given, (list, tuple)) or not all(
                c is None or isinstance(c, str) for c in given)):
            raise Refusal(f"{col}: a code is text, or a list of text codes; got {given!r}. Nothing was written.")
        lens[col] = [c.strip() for c in (given or ()) if c is not None and c.strip()]
    dbcore.validate_cols(data.keys(), _COLS, "insert_extraction")
    dbcore.check_jurisdiction(data.get("jurisdiction"), "add-extraction --jurisdiction")
    row = {k: v for k, v in data.items() if v is not None}

    # A BLANK IS NOT AN ABSENCE — normalise before anything reads these.
    for col in ("value_as_written",):
        if col in row and not str(row[col]).strip():
            del row[col]
    if "value_as_written" in row:
        row["value_as_written"] = str(row["value_as_written"]).strip()

    with dbcore.connect(dry_run) as conn:
        ref = dbcore.fold_ref(row.get("ref_id"))
        if not dbcore.exists(conn, "evidence_sources", "ref_id", ref):
            raise Refusal(
                f"ref_id {data.get('ref_id')!r} is not an admitted source. An extraction "
                f"is a reading OF a source; extract AFTER admission.\n"
                f"  db.py add-source ...")
        _refuse_tombstone(conn, ref, "add-extraction")
        row["ref_id"] = ref
        # AN EXTRACTION IS A READING. A source whose existence is not established
        # (verification_status UNVERIFIED or NULL, D-0157) was never obtained, and the
        # skill says never to describe it as read; a value attributed to it is a claim
        # about a document nobody held. Live rows already sit on such sources (derive:
        # SELECT COUNT(*) FROM source_value_extractions x JOIN evidence_sources e USING
        # (ref_id) WHERE COALESCE(e.verification_status,'') <> 'VERIFIED'); they are
        # history, and this refusal stops the next one.
        _vs = conn.execute("SELECT verification_status FROM evidence_sources WHERE ref_id=?",
                           (ref,)).fetchone()[0]
        if _vs != "VERIFIED":
            raise Refusal(
                f"add-extraction: {ref} is {_vs or 'NULL'}, not VERIFIED. An extraction is a "
                f"reading of a document this project obtained; a source whose standing is "
                f"not established cannot have been read. Retrieve and verify it first "
                f"(R10; db.py amend-source), or admit it UNVERIFIED and leave it unread. "
                f"Nothing was written.")

        # A slug guides what is searched, not what is read (scan contract, LED-195): no slug is
        # asked for here, and `source_slug_links` stays the admission record. A root_id names a
        # row of the registry (migration 114); an in-corpus root is root_ref_id.
        if row.get("root_id") is not None and not dbcore.exists(
                conn, "external_root_registry", "root_id", row["root_id"]):
            raise Refusal(
                f"root_id {row['root_id']!r} is not in external_root_registry. A root_id names an "
                f"external root; a root held in this corpus is --root-ref-id. Register the root "
                f"first with `db.py register-root`, then give its id here.")

        # --- the subject -----------------------------------------------------
        pid = row.get("parameter_id")
        if pid is None:
            raise Refusal(
                "--parameter-id is required: an extraction whose subject is unknown "
                "cannot reach the determination it exists to support (owner 2026-08-26, "
                "'the judgment object is the canonical parameter').")
        n_params = conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM base_parameters").fetchone()[0]
        if n_params == 0:
            raise Refusal(
                "`base_parameters` holds no rows, so NO parameter_id can be valid and a "
                "bare INSERT would fail with `FOREIGN KEY constraint failed` — a refusal "
                "that names neither the cause nor the fix (CLAUDE.md §4).\n"
                "Mint the subject first, from an adjudicated term:\n"
                "  db.py add-parameter --term-id TERM-NNN --quantity-kind K --quantity-kind-observation-id N --session ...")
        prow = conn.execute("SELECT status, merged_into FROM base_parameters "
                            "WHERE parameter_id=?", (pid,)).fetchone()
        if prow is None:
            raise Refusal(
                f"parameter_id {pid}: no such parameter. Mint one from a term:\n"
                f"  db.py add-parameter --term-id TERM-NNN --quantity-kind K --quantity-kind-observation-id N --session ...")
        if prow["status"] != "active":
            target = f" (merged into {prow['merged_into']})" if prow["merged_into"] else ""
            raise Refusal(
                f"parameter_id {pid} is {prow['status']}{target}, not active. Key the "
                f"extraction on the surviving parameter — a value filed under a folded "
                f"parameter is unreachable from the determination that replaced it.")

        # --- the reading record (R16, OR-11a) --------------------------------
        # The reading comes first and leaves a source_scans row; what it found is this
        # row. An extraction with no covering reading is consumed before it was read
        # (adversarial lens S4-sequence). `verified` additionally needs the reading to
        # be full-scope (OR-11a, owner 2026-10-29). Both were stated by the skill and
        # held by nothing; the live rows that lack a covering reading are history (derive
        # the verified ones: python3 scripts/audit/verified_scan_integrity.py).
        if _covering_scan(conn, ref, pid) is None:
            raise Refusal(
                f"add-extraction: no source_scans row covers {ref} for parameter {pid}. "
                f"Record the reading first -- db.py record-scan --ref-id {ref} --mode "
                f"catalogue (or --mode targeted --target-parameter-id {pid}) -- then "
                f"write what it found. Nothing was written.")
        if row.get("extraction_status") == "verified":
            _require_full_scan_for_verified(conn, ref, pid, "add-extraction")

        # --- the lenses ------------------------------------------------------
        if not any(lens.values()):
            raise Refusal(
                "an extraction must be stated in at least one lens (D-0182): pass one or "
                "more of --identity / --icf / --needs. A value attached to no "
                "lens is a value about nobody.")
        for col, codes in lens.items():
            dup = sorted({c for c in codes if codes.count(c) > 1})
            if dup:
                raise Refusal(f"{col}: {dup} given more than once in this call. A figure holds one live "
                              f"link per code. Nothing was written.")
            for code in codes:
                _require_lens_code(conn, col, code)

        # --- the claim -------------------------------------------------------
        claim_type = row.get("claim_type")
        value = row.get("claimed_value")
        figure_role = row.get("figure_role")
        # A DERIVED FIGURE HAS NO QUOTE OR LOCATOR OF ITS OWN (OD-40, delegated 2026-11-13): its words and its
        # place are its inputs', reached through its `derived_from` edges, each of which carries its input's
        # verified quote. A figure a source states in words is a claim row, never a derived one.
        if figure_role == "derived":
            if "claim_text" in row:
                raise Refusal(
                    "add-extraction: a derived figure carries no claim_text of its own: its words are its inputs', "
                    "reached through its derived_from edges (OD-40). A figure the source states in words is a claim "
                    "row (--figure-role claim); a computed one is written with db.py derive-extraction. "
                    "Nothing was written.")
